title: Retain household chat messages with anonymized authors on account deletion
owner_decision: Preserve messages sent in household chats, with the author anonymized.
classification: Confirmed contract mismatch fixed: deleting a member previously cascaded through their shared chat messages, contrary to the selected shared-history policy.

change.model: ChatMessage.user_id is nullable and references users with ON DELETE SET NULL.
change.migration: d6e7f8a9b0c1 changes existing PostgreSQL schemas. Downgrade refuses while anonymous messages exist, preserving retained content.
change.display: ChatMessage serialization uses the existing generic member label when no author remains.
change.attachments: Uploader-owned attachment rows and files are still removed after account deletion commits.

verification.pre_fix_reproduction: On a fresh database at the prior Alembic head, test_native_admin_deletion_removes_rows_and_retries_owned_file_cleanup failed because the shared message had been cascade-deleted.
verification.schema: scripts/upgrade_test_schema.py upgraded the fresh test database through the new migration; python -m alembic check reported no new upgrade operations.
verification.rollback: Clean downgrade and re-upgrade passed. With a retained NULL-author message present, downgrade refused and both that row and the Alembic head were preserved.
verification.database: Disposable oneirodexchatpre_test on the loopback PostgreSQL 17.6 review container; dropped after verification. Process-scoped DATABASE_URL/TEST_DATABASE_URL overrides left the root .env unchanged.

limits: Verification uses the current schema, not an operator's deployed schema.
Chat retention was implemented only for household ChatMessage rows; other retained user-authored free-text fields still need classification.
